[^26]: Red cinnabar colophon and heading at the foot of fol. 5v introducing the second psalm of the Praises (Lauds): 'аллилоугіа • ѱалѡмь рм҃ѳ' ('Alleluia. Psalm 149 [LXX Ps. 149]').

[^27]: Antiphonal refrains in cinnabar vermilion ink during Psalm 149: 'хвала тебѣ ст҃ыи ѻч҃е' ('Praise unto Thee, O Holy Father!') after v. 1, and 'пощади ны ги҃' ('Spare us, O Lord!') after v. 6.

[^28]: Incipit of Psalm 150 (LXX Ps. 150) opening with a two-line decorative initial 'Х' and marginal Cyrillic numeral 'рн҃' (150). The choral refrain 'тебѣ жїи подоба пѣ[снь]' is an abbreviated scribal typesetting for 'Тебѣ подобаетъ пѣснь, Боже' ('Unto Thee is due a hymn, O God!').

[^29]: In Psalm 150:2, Fiol inserts the cinnabar refrain 'слава показавшоумѹ свѣтъ' ('Glory to Him Who hath shown the light!'), anticipating the solemn morning proclamation that concludes Matins and introduces the Doxology.

[^30]: The rubric at the foot of fol. 6v establishes the liturgical distinction between festal/Sunday Matins (wherein the Great Doxology is solemnly chanted: 'поетсѧ славословіе великое') and ordinary daily Matins (wherein the Small Doxology is recited rapidly: 'сіе гл҃етсѧ ѡт пѣвца по скоро').

[^31]: The Doxology text on fol. 7r transitions immediately into the traditional morning biblical verses: LXX Ps. 89:1, LXX Ps. 40:5, LXX Ps. 142:9–10, and LXX Ps. 35:10.

[^32]: Folio 7v line 12 preserves the typographical error 'текбѣ' for 'тебѣ' ('текбѣ побаеть пѣніе' / 'Unto Thee is due a song'), demonstrating the mechanical hand-set character of Fiol’s 1491 Krakow Cyrillic font.

[^33]: Concluding rubrics for Matins on fol. 7v: after the Trisagion and Troparion, the deacon or priest intones the Litany of Fervent Supplication ('Помилуй насъ, Боже...') followed by the prayer of head-bowing ('Господи святый, иже въ вышнихъ живый...').

[^34]: Signature 'г҃і' (13) at the bottom center of fol. 8r marks the opening leaf of the thirteenth quire. The leaf records the dismissal dialogue: the priest proclaims 'Сый благословенъ Христосъ Богъ нашъ...', the reader responds 'Утверди, Боже, вѣру христіанскую...', followed by the 'More honorable than the Cherubim' and the shortened dismissal ('съкрѫшеныи ѡтпоустъ').

[^35]: Rubric on fol. 8r for daily Matins when the Great Doxology is not sung: the morning litany ('Let us complete our morning prayer...') is followed by the Aposticha with its morning verses (LXX Ps. 89:14, 17) and the hymn 'It is good to give thanks unto the Lord...' (LXX Ps. 91:2–3).

[^36]: Monastic penitential ending for daily Matins on fol. 8v: the troparion is followed by the daily Theotokion 'Въ церкви стояще...', 40 repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy', and the prayer 'O Heavenly King...'.

[^37]: The monastic dismissal concludes with the Prayer of St. Ephrem the Syrian ('Господи и Владыко живота моего...') with three great prostrations and twelve reverences (metanias). The First Hour is immediately introduced with a calligraphic ligatured heading in cinnabar vermilion ink: 'И ꙖБИѤ НАЧИНАЄМЬ .А҃.' ('And immediately we begin the First Hour').

[^38]: The First Hour opens on fol. 9r with Psalm 5 (LXX Ps. 5:2–11), marked by a two-line red initial 'Г' ('Глаголы моя внуши, Господи' / 'Give ear unto my words, O Lord').

[^39]: In LXX Ps. 5:11–13, the archaic Church Slavonic witness preserves the exact Septuagint syntax, concluding with the martial metaphor of divine favour as a crowning shield ('оружіемъ благоволенія вѣнчалъ еси насъ').

[^40]: Cinnabar heading on fol. 9v: 'мл҃тва мѡѵсеѡва чл҃ка бж҃іа • п҃ѳ' ('A Prayer of Moses, the man of God. Psalm 89 [LXX Ps. 89]'). In verse 5, the print witnesses the archaic form 'лѣще бѫдоуть' ('their trivialities shall be years'), rendering Greek τὰ ἐξουδενώματα αὐτῶν ἔτη ἔσονται.

[^41]: Folio 10r signature 'г҃і' (13) in the bottom right margin designates the third leaf of quire 13. In LXX Ps. 89:10, Fiol renders τὰ ἔτη ἡμῶν ὡς ἀράхνη ἐмеλέτων as 'лѣта наша ꙗко паоучина пооучаахѫ сѧ' ('our years were considered like a spider’s web').

[^42]: The Slavonic text preserves the ancient Septuagint translation of LXX Ps. 89:10: 'яко наиде кротость на ны и накажемся' ('for mildness hath come upon us, and we shall be chastened'), rendering Greek ὅти ἐпῆλθεν пραΰτηѕ ἐφ' ἡмᾶѕ кαὶ пαιδευθηѕόмеθа.

[^43]: In LXX Ps. 89:12, the archaic translation 'и окованыя сердцемъ въ мудрости' ('and those who are shackled in heart in wisdom') faithfully reflects the Greek τοὺς пεпεδημένουѕ τῇ κаρδίᾳ ἐν ѕοφίᾳ.

[^44]: Leaf p21 concludes Psalm 89 (LXX Ps. 89:17) with the double petition for the confirmation of human works: 'и дѣла рѫкъ нашихъ исправи на насъ, и дѣло рѫкъ нашихъ исправи', reflecting the ancient Septuagint doublet καὶ τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν ἡμῶν κατεύθυνον ἐφ' ἡμᾶς, καὶ τὸ ἔργον τῶν χειρῶν ἡμῶν κατεύθυνον.

[^45]: Leaf p21 witnesses the incipit of Psalm 100 (LXX Ps. 100) with a cinnabar cross, heading 'ѱалѡ[мъ] р҃', marginal Cyrillic numeral 'р҃' (100), and a three-line red initial 'М' ('Милость и судъ пою Тебѣ, Господи...'). Psalm 100 serves as the concluding psalm of the First Hour triad (Psalms 5, 89, 100).

[^46]: Cinnabar rubrics on fol. 11r specify the Lenten morning versicles of the First Hour: 'Заутра услыши гласъ мои...' (LXX Ps. 5:3–4) chanted in Tone 6 with two appointed stichoi. The rubric prescribes that during the Great Fast (Forty Days) it is chanted 'велегласно' (with a solemn raised voice), whereas in the lesser fasting periods it is recited 'низко' (quietly/humbly).

[^47]: Folio 11r contains the morning Theotokion 'Что тя наречемъ, о обрадованная...' ('What shall we name thee, O full of grace?') accompanied by three prostrations.

[^48]: The concluding biblical versicles of the First Hour on fol. 11r: LXX Ps. 118:133–135 ('Стопы моя направи...') followed by LXX Ps. 70:8 ('Да исполнятся уста моя похвалы Твоея, Господи...'). The vermilion marker 'г҃д' in line 18 marks the abbreviation for the Lord's Name.

[^49]: Folio 11v gives the ordinary troparion of the First Hour in Tone 4 ('Скоро предвари, прежде даже не поработимся врагомъ...'), followed by the penitential kontakion 'Премудрости наставниче...' and the Theotokion 'Преславную Христову Матерь...'.

[^50]: Quire signature 'д҃і' (14) at the foot of fol. 12r marks the opening leaf of the fourteenth quire. The dismissal dialogue follows the monastic ordo: 40 repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy', the universal Prayer of the Hours ('Иже на всякое время...'), the Trisagion, and the Prayer of St. Ephrem with three prostrations and twelve metanias.

[^51]: Solemn concluding prayer of the First Hour on fol. 12r: 'Христе, свѣте истинный...' ('O Christ, the true Light, Who enlightenest and sanctifiest every man that comes into the world...').

[^52]: Cinnabar heading on fol. 12r: 'Межоучасіе .а҃. часа' ('The Inter-Hour of the First Hour'). In the ancient Studite and early Jerusalem monastic Typika preserved in 15th-century Ruthenian and South Slavic codices, inter-hours (междочасія) were appointed during fasting seasons between the primary canonical hours.

[^53]: Cinnabar heading for Psalm 91 (LXX Ps. 91) on fol. 12v: 'ѱлѡ[мъ] • пѣсникъ • дн҃ь сѫботы • ч҃а' ('A Psalm, a song for the Sabbath day; 91'). In verse 1, 'Бл҃го есть исповѣдати сѧ гв҃и' renders Greek Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ.

[^54]: In LXX Ps. 91:11 on fol. 13r, the archaic Church Slavonic witness preserves the biblical beast 'инорогъ' (unicorn / monoceros: καὶ ὑψωθήσεται ὡς μονοκέρωτος τὸ κέρας μου) and renders the flourish of old age as 'въ елеи маститѣ' (in rich/fat oil: ἐν ἐλαίῳ πίονι).

[^55]: Cinnabar heading for the third psalm of the Mesohorion on fol. 13v: 'Въ дн҃ь иже къ сѫботѣ хвала пѣсни дв҃двы :~ ч҃в' (Psalm 92 / LXX Ps. 92, 'For the day before the Sabbath, a song of praise of David; 92').

[^56]: Concluding penitential troparia of the Mesohorion on fol. 13v: 'Помилуй насъ, Господи, помилуй насъ, всякаго отвѣта недоумѣюще...' ('Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, lacking any defense...').

[^57]: The concluding Theotokion of the Mesohorion on fol. 14r: 'Милосердія двери отверзи намъ, благословенная Богородице...' ('Open unto us the door of compassion, O blessed Theotokos...'), followed by 30 repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy' and the Prayer of St. Ephrem.

[^58]: First Prayer of the Inter-Hour of the First Hour on fol. 14r: 'Боже вѣчный, безначальный и присносущный источниче...' ('O Eternal and Unoriginate God, Ever-Existing Fountain...').

[^59]: Cinnabar marginal numeral and heading 'в҃ мл҃тва' ('Second Prayer') on fol. 14v introducing the morning supplication: 'Посылаяй свѣтъ и идетъ, возсіяй солнце на праведныя же и неправедныя...' ('O Thou Who sendest forth the light, and it goes...').

[^60]: The Second Prayer of the Mesohorion on fol. 15r concludes with an ecphonesis of praise unto the Holy Trinity: 'Твое бо есть еже миловати и спасти ны, Боже нашъ, и Тебѣ славу возсылаемъ, Отцу и Сыну и Святому Духу, нынѣ и присно [и во вѣки вѣковъ. Аминь]'.

[^61]: Monumental decorative heading in vermilion cinnabar display capitals on fol. 15r: 'ЧА́СЪ • Г҃ • БЛ҃ГОСЛОВИВШЮ ИЄРЕЮ' ('The Third Hour: When the priest hath given the blessing'). This marks the canonical opening of the Third Hour (Terce) with the priestly blessing.

[^62]: Opening psalm of the Third Hour on fol. 15r: Psalm 16 (LXX Ps. 16:1–4), introduced by the cinnabar inscription 'мл҃тва дв҃два • ѕ҃і' ('A Prayer of David. 16') with a large red initial 'О' ('Услыши, Господи, правду мою...').

[^63]: Folio 15v witnesses the central verses of Psalm 16 (LXX Ps. 16:4–9). In verse 8, 'съхрани мя г҃и ꙗко зѣницю ѡка' translates Septuagint φύλαξόν με ὡς κόραν ὀφθαλμοῦ, and the description of the adversaries 'ѡстрастьшихъ мя' renders Greek τῶν ταλαιπωρησάντων με.

[^64]: Folio 15v preserves the graphic simile in LXX Ps. 16:12–13: 'ѡбьꙗша мя ꙗко львъ готовъ на ловъ • и ꙗко скѵмень ѡбитаꙗ въ скровищихъ' (ὑπέλαβόν με ὡσεὶ λέων ἕτοιμος εἰς θήραν καὶ ὡσεὶ σκύμνος οἰκῶν ἐν ἀποκρύφοις). The imperative 'прѣдвари хъ [ꙗ] и запни имь' renders Greek πρόφθασον αὐτοὺς καὶ ὑποσκέλισον αὐτούς.

[^65]: Folio 16r gives the concluding verses of Psalm 16 (LXX Ps. 16:14–15). The Church Slavonic reading 'насытиша сѧ свиніихъ' directly reflects the Septuagint ἐχορτάσθησαν ὑείων (swine's flesh / pork) rather than the Masoretic reading 'sons', testifying to the codex's strict fidelity to the ancient Byzantine-Greek textual recension.

[^66]: Cinnabar heading 'ѱлѡ҃ к҃д' on fol. 16r introduces Psalm 24 (LXX Ps. 24), an alphabetical acrostic psalm in the original Hebrew. Schweipolt Fiol preserves the liturgical consciousness of this structure by rubricating the initial letters of several strophes in cinnabar ('И', 'Д', 'П', 'И').

[^67]: Folio 16v witnesses LXX Ps. 24:16: 'призри на мя и помилоуи мя ꙗко единородъ и нищь есмь азъ', precisely rendering Greek ἐπίβλεψον ἐπ' ἐμὲ καὶ ἐλέησόν με, ὅτι μονογενὴς καὶ πτωχός εἰμι ἐγώ.

[^68]: Cinnabar inscription 'ѱлѡ[мъ] дв҃двъ н҃' on fol. 17r introduces Psalm 50 (LXX Ps. 50), the universal penitential psalm of David, decorated with a four-line cinnabar initial 'П' ('Помилуй мя, Боже...'). Psalm 50 is appointed as the third and concluding psalm of the Third Hour triad (Psalms 16, 24, 50).

[^69]: In LXX Ps. 50:8 on fol. 17r, the phrase 'безвѣстьнаа и таиннаа прѣмѫдрости твоеꙗ явилъ ми еси' renders Greek τὰ ἄδηλα καὶ τὰ κρύφια τῆς σοφίας σου ἐδήλωσάς μοι.

[^70]: Folio 17v witnesses LXX Ps. 50:14: 'и д[у]хѡ[мъ] вл[дч]ьнѡ[мъ] ѹтвръди мя', translating Septuagint καὶ πνεύματι ἡγεμονικῷ στήρισόν με ('uphold me with a guiding / princely Spirit').

[^71]: Folio 18r carries quire signature 'е҃і' (15) at the lower right margin, marking the start of quire 15. The cinnabar rubrics prescribe the Lenten troparion of the Third Hour in Tone 6 ('Господи, Иже Пресвятый Твой Духъ въ третій часъ Апостоломъ Твоимъ пославый...') together with verses 12 and 13 of Psalm 50.

[^72]: Folio 18r contains the ancient Theotokion of the Third Hour: 'Богородице, Ты еси лоза истинная...' ('O Theotokos, thou art the true Vine...'), followed by the dismissal verses from LXX Ps. 67:20–21 ('Господь Богъ благословенъ...') and the Pentecost Troparion in Tone 8 ('Благословенъ еси, Христе Боже нашъ...').

[^73]: Folio 18v witnesses the conclusion of the Pentecost Troparion, followed by the Pentecost Kontakion ('Егда съшедъ языки размѣси...', Tone 8) and the monumental Kontakion to the Mother of God ('Възбранной воеводѣ побѣдителная...', Tone 8).

[^74]: The solemn concluding prayer of the Third Hour on fol. 18v: 'Владыко Боже, Отче Вседержителю, и Господи Сыне Единородный, Іисусе Христе, и Святый Душе...' ('O Master God, Father Almighty...'), traditionally attributed to the 4th-century martyr Saint Mardarios of Sebaste.

[^75]: Cinnabar heading on fol. 19r: 'Межѹчасіе .г҃. го часа' ('The Inter-Hour of the Third Hour'). The Mesohorion of Terce opens with Psalm 29 (LXX Ps. 29, 'ѱаломь давыдовъ , к҃ѳ :~') introduced by a large red initial 'В' ('Вознесу Тя, Господи, яко подъятъ мя еси...').

[^76]: Folio 19v introduces the second psalm of the Mesohorion with cinnabar heading 'ѱалѡмь дв҃двъ разоумь л҃а :~' (Psalm 31 / LXX Ps. 31, Maskil of David: 'Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven...'). In verse 4, 'възврати сѧ на страсть егда ѹнзе ми трънь' renders Greek ἐστράφην εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν ἐν τῷ ἐμπαγῆναι ἄканθαν.

[^77]: Folio 20r bears quire signature 'ѕ҃і' (16) at the lower right margin, marking the sixteenth quire. The leaf concludes Psalm 31 with the warning against unreasoning stubborness ('не будѣте яко конь и мьскъ...' - LXX Ps. 31:9) and the exultation of the righteous ('Възвеселитеся о Господѣ...').

[^78]: Cinnabar incipit of Psalm 60 on fol. 20r: 'въ конець въ пѣснехъ, ѱалѡмь дв҃двъ • ѯ҃ :~' (LXX Ps. 60, Εἰς τὸ τέλος, ἐν ὕμνοις· τῷ Δαυΐδ: 'Hear my supplication, O God; attend unto my prayer...'), opening the third psalm of the Inter-Hour of the Third Hour.

[^79]: Folio 20v concludes Psalm 60 (LXX Ps. 60:3–9), the third psalm of the Inter-Hour of the Third Hour. Verse 5 witnesses 'въселю сѧ въ селѣ твоемь въ вѣкы' (Greek κατασκηνώσω ἐν τῷ σκηνώματί σου εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας), and verse 7 expresses the royal petition 'днь на днь цр҃ю приложиши' (ἡμέρας ἐφ' ἡμέρας βασιλεῖ προσθήσεις), reflecting the Byzantine court liturgical milieu embedded in the liturgical Psalter.

[^80]: Folio 20v gives the cinnabar rubric prescribing the Trisagion and troparia after the Lord's Prayer in Tone 4: 'Б҃е ѡ́ц҃ь нашихъ твора[и] присно с нами по твоемоу смотреніоу...' ('O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy dispensation...'), the ancient Troparion of the Holy Fathers and Saints, translating Greek Ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιῶν ἀεὶ μεθ' ἡμῶν κατὰ τὴν σὴν ἐπιείκειαν.

[^81]: Folios 20v–21r witness the common Troparion to the Holy Martyrs in Tone 4: 'Мѫченици Твои, Господи...'. At the page turn, the reading 'и ѹпраздниша бѣсовъ / дль немощнаꙗ шатаніа' preserves an archaic Slavonic rendering of Greek καὶ συντρίβουσι τὰ τῶν δαιμόνων ἀνίσχυρα θράση, where 'дль' represents an abbreviation or contraction for 'дѣла' (deeds) or 'дерзости' (insolence/ravings).

[^82]: Folio 21r witnesses the ancient Tone 4 Theotokion of the Third Hour inter-hour: 'Стѣна непобѣдимая намъ христіаномъ ты еси, Богородице Дѣво...' ('An invincible wall art thou unto us Christians, O Virgin Theotokos...'). The rubric specifies 'Г҃и помилоуи • л҃ •' (Lord, have mercy, 30 times), reflecting early monastic usage for the mesohoria, followed by the Prayer of Saint Ephrem with three great prostrations.

[^83]: Cinnabar attribution on fol. 21r: 'посе сію мл҃[тву] ст҃го в[асиліа] сіа' ('after this, this Prayer of Saint Basil'). This solemn prayer of Saint Basil the Great ('Господи Боже нашъ, Иже Свой миръ давый человѣкомъ...'; Greek Κύριε ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ὁ τὴν σὴν εἰρήνην δοὺς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις...) is an ancient hallmark of the Sabaite and Studite Horologia for the Inter-Hour of the Third Hour.

[^84]: Folio 21v bears a monumental cinnabar title in elaborate Cyrillic display ligature lettering (vyaz'): 'НАЧАЛО ШЕСТОГО ЧАСА' ('The Beginning of the Sixth Hour'). The Sixth Hour commemorates the sixth hour of the day (noon), when Christ was nailed to the Cross at Golgotha.

[^85]: Cinnabar rubric on fol. 21v: 'пр[ии]дете поклоним сѧ • г҃ • ѱлѡ[мъ] дв҃двъ • н҃г •' introduces Psalm 53 (LXX Ps. 53: 'Боже, въ имя Твое спаси мя...'), opening with a four-line cinnabar initial 'Б'. Psalm 53 is the first psalm of the Sixth Hour triad (Psalms 53, 54, 90).

[^86]: Folio 22r concludes Psalm 53 and introduces the second psalm of the Sixth Hour with cinnabar rubric 'въ конець [въ] пѣніи разоумъ дв҃двъ' and red marginal numeral 'н҃д' (Psalm 54 / LXX Ps. 54: Εἰς τὸ τέλος, ἐν ὕμνοις· συνέσεως τῷ Δαυΐδ: 'Give ear unto my prayer, O God, and despise not my supplication...').

[^87]: Folio 22v preserves David's prophetic lament over treachery in LXX Ps. 54:14–15: 'ты же чл҃че равнодѹшне, вл[д]ко мои зна́емыи...' (Greek σὺ δὲ ἄνθρωπε ἰσόψυχε, ἡγεμών μου καὶ γνωστέ μου). Christian liturgical and Patristic exegesis unanimously interprets this passage as a typology of Judas Iscariot's betrayal of Christ, fittingly chanted at the Sixth Hour of the Passion.

[^88]: Cinnabar heading on fol. 23r: 'хвала пѣни давыдовы :~ ч҃ :~' introduces Psalm 90 (LXX Ps. 90: Αἶνος ᾠδῆς τῷ Δαυΐδ), adorned with a four-line cinnabar braided initial 'Ж' ('Живый въ помощи Вышняго...'). Psalm 90 concludes the fixed psalm triad of the Sixth Hour.

[^89]: Folio 23v witnesses LXX Ps. 90:5–6 with the graphic phrase 'ѿ срѣща и́ бѣса полоуденьнаго' (Greek ἀπὸ συμπτώματος καὶ δαιμονίου меσημβρινοῦ: 'from mishap and the noonday demon'), directly invoking divine protection during the midday heat and the mystical hour of the Crucifixion.

[^90]: Folio 24r gives the dismissal rubrics and the classic Lenten troparion of the Sixth Hour in Tone 2: 'Иже въ шестии день же и часъ на Крестѣ пригвоздивый...' ('Thou Who on the sixth day and hour didst nail to the Cross the sin which daring Adam committed in Paradise...'), accompanied by psalm verses from LXX Ps. 54:17–18.

[^91]: Folio 24r witnesses the beloved Theotokion of the Sixth Hour: 'Яко не имамы дерзновенія...' ('Because we have no boldness by reason of our many sins...'), invoking the boundless efficacy of maternal intercession before Christ ('много бо можетъ молитва матерняя къ умоленію Владыки').

[^92]: Folio 24v records the penitential psalm versicle from LXX Ps. 78:8–9 ('Скоро да предварятъ ны щедроты Твоя, Господи...'), followed by the Tone 2 troparia of the Cross: 'Спасеніе содѣлалъ еси посредѣ земли, Христе Боже...' and 'Пречистому Твоему образу покланяемся, Благій...'.

[^93]: Folio 24v gives the opening of the tender Tone 2 Theotokion: 'Милосердія сущи источникъ, милости сподоби насъ, Богородице...' ('Being a wellspring of compassion, vouchsafe mercy unto us, O Theotokos...').

[^94]: Folio 25r bears the cinnabar heading 'Междючасіе шестого часа' ('The Inter-Hour of the Sixth Hour') and opens its first psalm, Psalm 55 (LXX Ps. 55: 'Помилуй мя, Боже, яко попра мя человѣкъ...'), introduced by a three-line cinnabar initial 'П'.

[^95]: Folio 25v concludes Psalm 55 (LXX Ps. 55:7–13), completing the first psalm of the Inter-Hour of the Sixth Hour (Междючасіе шестого часа). The witness preserves David's vow: 'въ мнѣ, Боже, молитвы, яже воздахъ хвалѣ Твое́и' (Greek Ἐν ἐμοί, ὁ Θεός, εὐχαί, ἃς ἀποδώσω αἰνέσεώς σου), declaring deliverance from death and walking before the Lord in the light of the living.

[^96]: Folio 25v bears the cinnabar rubric 'вконьць ѡ́ нерастлѣніи дв҃дѹ ѱлѡ҃ н҃ѕ :~' introducing Psalm 56 (LXX Ps. 56: Εἰς τὸ τέλος, μὴ διαφθεῖραι· τῷ Δαυΐδ εἰς στηλογραφίαν), the second psalm of the Sixth Hour Inter-Hour, adorned with a four-line cinnabar initial 'П' ('Помилуй мя, Боже...').

[^97]: Folio 26r concludes Psalm 56 (LXX Ps. 56:4–12) with David's morning praise ('востани псалтирю и гусли, востану рано...') and introduces the third psalm with the cinnabar rubric 'въ конець ѱалѡмь дв҃двъ • въ спѡминаніе въ е́же сп҃сти мя :~ ѯ҃ѳ :~' (LXX Ps. 69: Εἰς τὸ τέλος, τῷ Δαυΐδ, εἰς ἀνάмνησιν, εἰς τὸ σῶσαί με Κύριον).

[^98]: Folio 26v opens Psalm 69 (LXX Ps. 69:2: 'Боже, въ помощь мою вонми...'), introduced with a four-line cinnabar initial 'Б'. This supplication concludes the psalm triad of the Sixth Hour Inter-Hour.

[^99]: Folio 26v preserves the archaic liturgical rubric: 'Сла́ и́ нн҃ѣ • безъ аллилу́іа • тр[ъ]стое • и́ де • г҃ • по ѡ́[т]че нашь • тропарѣ сіа гл҃а • а҃ •' ('Glory... Both now... without Alleluia. Trisagion. And 3 metanias. After Our Father, these troparia in Tone 1:'). This rubric explicitly omits the customary threefold Alleluia at the conclusion of the psalm triad, prescribing the Troparion of the Cross: 'Спаси, Господи, люди Твоя...' (Tone 1) and the Troparion to the Holy Martyrs: 'Страстьми святыхъ, иже по Тебѣ пріяша...'.

[^100]: Folio 27r witnesses the concluding Theotokion of the Sixth Hour Inter-Hour: 'Молитвами, Господи, всѣхъ святыхъ Твоихъ и Богородицы, Твой миръ даждь намъ, и помилуй насъ, яко Единъ Щедръ' ('By the prayers of all Thy Saints, O Lord, and of the Theotokos, grant us Thy peace...').

[^101]: Folio 27r provides the monastic dismissal rubrics for the Inter-Hour: thirty repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy' ('г҃и помилоуи • л҃ •'), the hymn 'More honorable than the Cherubim', priestly blessing ('попъ: святи за молитвъ святыхъ отецъ нашихъ'), and the Prayer of Saint Ephrem ('Господи и Владыко живота моего...') with three great prostrations.

[^102]: Folio 27r bears the cinnabar attribution 'мл҃тва великаго василіа :~' introducing the solemn prayer of Saint Basil the Great ('Боже и Господи силъ, и всея твари Содѣтелю...'; Greek Κύριε ὁ Θεὸς τῶν δυνάмеων, καὶ πάσης κτίσεως δημιουργέ...), which crowns the Sixth Hour and its Inter-Hour in early Sabaite and Studite tradition.

[^103]: Folio 27v bears a monumental cinnabar title in liturgical display script marking a major landmark in the Horologion: 'Начало типикомъ • еже есть ѡ́бѣдница •' ('The Beginning of the Typika, which is the Obednitsa'), followed by the blessing 'Благословенъ еси, Господи' and Psalm 102 (LXX Ps. 102: 'Благослови, душе моя, Господа...'), the First Antiphon of the Typika.

[^104]: Folio 28v records the Second Antiphon of the Typika: Psalm 145 (LXX Ps. 145: 'Хвали, душе моя, Господа...'), introduced with the cinnabar inscription 'а́ллилу́іа а́ггеꙗ и́ захаріꙗ' (Greek Ἀλληλούϊα, Ἁγγαίου καὶ Ζαχαρίου) and the red numeral 'р҃ме' in the margin, beginning with a four-line cinnabar initial 'Х'.

[^105]: Folio 29r witnesses the classic Byzantine Christological hymn attributed to Emperor Justinian I (c. 528): 'Единородный Сыне и Слове Божій...' (Greek Ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς καὶ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ...), chanted at the conclusion of the Second Antiphon of the Typika.

[^106]: Folio 29v introduces the Third Antiphon of the Typika: the Evangelical Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–12), preceded by the refrain of the Good Thief (Luke 23:42): 'Въ царствіи си егда пріидеши, помяни насъ, Господи' ('In Thy Kingdom remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom').

[^107]: Folio 29v prescribes the liturgical lessons of the Typika with the concise rubric: 'Таже Апостолъ и Евангеліе' ('Then the Epistle and Gospel'), followed by the threefold repetition of the Thief's prayer addressed successively to the Lord, the Master, and the Holy One ('Помяни насъ, Господи... Помяни насъ, Владыко... Помяни насъ, Святый...').

[^108]: Folios 29v–30r record the angelic Trisagion hymn of the Typika: 'Ликъ небесный поетъ Тя и глаголетъ: Святъ, Святъ, Святъ, Господь Саваоѳъ, исполнь небо и землю славы Твоея', interspersed with Psalm 33:6 ('Приступите къ Нему и просвѣтитеся...').

[^109]: Folio 30r bears the cinnabar heading 'Исповѣданіе православныя вѣры' ('The Confession of the Orthodox Faith'), introducing the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Symbol of Faith: 'Вѣрую во единаго Бога, Отца, Вседержителя...' ('I believe in one God, the Father Almighty...'), adorned with a four-line cinnabar initial 'В'.

[^110]: Folio 30v concludes the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Symbol of Faith (Confessio Fidei) begun on fol. 30r, witnessing the Christological clauses on the Ascension, Session at the right hand of the Father, and Second Coming ('пакы грядущаго съ славою судити живымъ и мертвымъ'), the Pneumatological article on the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father ('иже отъ Отца исходящаго'), the Ecclesiological mark of the One Holy Catholic and Apostolic Church, and the resurrection of the dead. It is immediately followed by the ancient Byzantine Penitential Supplication ('Ѡслаби, остави, отпусти, прости, Боже, согрѣшенія наша...'; Greek Ἄνες, ἄφες, συγχώρησον, ὁ Θεός, τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν...), recited prostrate at the conclusion of the Typika.

[^111]: Folio 31r witnesses the conclusion of the prayer of remission and sets forth the weekly cycle of kontakia (кондаки на дни седмицы) for the Typika: Monday to the Bodiless Powers ('Архистратизи Божіи...'), Tuesday to the Forerunner ('Неплоды днесь...'), Wednesday and Friday to the Cross ('Вознесыйся на крестъ волею...'), Thursday to the Apostles and St. Nicholas ('Твердыя и боговѣщанныя...'), and Saturday to All Saints and the Departed ('Яко начатки естества...'), concluding with the Kontakion of the Departed ('Со святыми упокой, Христе...') and the solemn Marian Theotokion 'Заступнице христіаномъ непостыдная' (Greek Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν ἀκαταίσχυντε).

[^112]: Folio 31v provides comprehensive rubrics distinguishing the festal, daily, and Lenten celebrations of the Typika. On Feasts of the Lord, a single festal kontakion is prescribed; on simple weekdays, the kontakion of the day and for the departed; on feasts of celebrated saints, the saint's kontakion followed by the Theotokion. In Great Lent, forty repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy' are appointed, followed by the Prayer of Saint Ephrem the Syrian ('Господи и Владыко живота моего...') with three great prostrations and twelve metanias, concluding with the solemn Sabaite Prayer to the Most Holy Trinity ('Пресвятая Троице единосущная, неодержимая державо...'; Greek Παναγία Τριάς, ἡ ὁμοούσιος δύναμις, ἡ ἀδιαίρετος βασιλεία...).

[^113]: Folio 32r completes the Sabaite Trinitarian Prayer with the liturgical acclamation 'Единъ Святъ, Единъ Господь, Іисусъ Христосъ, въ славу Бога Отца' (Greek Εἷς ἅγιος, εἷς Κύριος, Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ Πατρός), the threefold 'Буди имя Господне благословено от нынѣ и до вѣка', and introduces Psalm 33 (LXX Ps. 33: 'Благословлю Господа на всяко время...'), the traditional thanksgiving psalm chanted at the conclusion of the Typika and during the distribution of the antidoron.

[^114]: Folio 32v continues Psalm 33 (LXX Ps. 33:10–21), preserving the classic didactic verses on the fear of the Lord, the restraint of speech ('удръжи языкъ свой отъ зла...'), and God's proximity to the broken-hearted ('близъ Господь сокрушеныхъ сердцемъ, и смиренныя духомъ спасетъ').

[^115]: Folio 33r concludes Psalm 33 (LXX Ps. 33:21–23) and presents the rubric for the monastic dismissal and procession to the refectory: 'Таже по семъ отпустъ. Идуще на трапезу глаголи сей псаломъ 144' ('Then after this the dismissal. Going to the refectory, recite this Psalm 144'). It introduces David's psalm of praise (LXX Ps. 144: 'Вознесу Тя, Боже мой, Царю мой...'), beginning with an ornate four-line initial 'В'.

[^116]: Folio 33v continues Psalm 144 (LXX Ps. 144:8–18), including the canonical Byzantine pre-prandial verses chanted before the meal: 'Очи всѣхъ на Тя уповаютъ, и Ты даеши пищу имъ въ благо время; отверзаеши Ты руку Твою, и насыщаеши всяко животно благоволенія' (LXX Ps. 144:15–16; Greek Οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ πάντων εἰς σὲ ἐλπίζουσι, καὶ σὺ δίδως τὴν τροφὴν αὐτῶν ἐν εὐκαιρίᾳ...).

[^117]: Folio 34r completes Psalm 144 (LXX Ps. 144:18–21) and witnesses a precious 15th-century monastic Typikon rubric governing the liturgical order of the procession from the church to the refectory (трапеза): the officiating priest leads, followed by the hegumen, then the hieromonks, and finally the brethren, walking in single file in total silence ('два два в рядъ не ходя, но жедутъ единъ по единому'). At the refectory table, the Lord's Prayer is recited, and the hegumen blesses the food with the ancient formula: 'Христе Боже, благослови ястіе и питіе рабомъ своимъ...'.

[^118]: Folio 34v details the refectory observance: monastic reading by the lector during the meal, strict silence enjoined according to patristic tradition ('съ многимъ млъчаніемъ по преданію святыхъ отецъ'), the post-prandial thanksgiving prayer ('Благословенъ Богъ милуяй и питаяй насъ отъ юности нашея...'; Greek Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός, ὁ ἐλεῶν καὶ τρέφων ἡμᾶς ἐκ νεότητος ἡμῶν...), and the concluding dialogue where the cellarer (келарь / cellaronarius) asks the community's forgiveness and blessing.

[^119]: Folio 35r opens the Office of the Ninth Hour (Часъ Девятый) with a monumental cinnabar display rubric: 'ЧАСЪ Ѳ҃. СИЦЕ ПОЕМЪ ЕГДА особь другыхъ часовъ, по благословеніи іереа, начинаемъ...' ('The Ninth Hour: We chant thus when sung apart from other hours...'), followed by the Opening Prayers and Psalm 83 (LXX Ps. 83: 'Коль возлюбленна селенія Твоя, Господи силъ...'; Greek Ὡς ἀγαπητὰ τὰ σκηνώματά σου, Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων...).

[^120]: Folio 35v witnesses the concluding verses of Psalm 83 (LXX Ps. 83:7–13), celebrating the blessedness of them that dwell in the house of God and go from strength to strength, followed by the opening of Psalm 84 (LXX Ps. 84:1–4; 'Благоволилъ еси, Господи, землю Твою...'), appointed at the Ninth Hour.

[^121]: Folio 36r completes Psalm 84 (LXX Ps. 84:5–14), featuring the messianic and incarnational verses on mercy and truth meeting, and righteousness looking down from heaven ('Милость и истина срѣтостася, правда и миръ облобызастася...'; Greek Ἔλεος καὶ ἀλήθεια συνήντησαν, δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη κατεφίλησαν...). It introduces the third psalm of the Ninth Hour, the Prayer of David, Psalm 85 (LXX Ps. 85:1–2; 'Приклони, Господи, ухо Твое, и услыши мя...').

[^122]: Folio 36v continues Psalm 85 (LXX Ps. 85:2–13), preserving the humble supplications for Divine mercy and guidance, the confession of God's solitary wonder-working power above all false gods ('яко велій еси Ты и творяй чудеса, Ты еси Богъ единъ'), and thanksgiving for deliverance from the lowest hades.

[^123]: Folio 37r concludes Psalm 85 (LXX Ps. 85:14–17), records the concluding metanias and daily troparion rubrics, and introduces the solemn penitential Troparia of the Ninth Hour appointed during the Fasts in Tone 8 ('Иже въ девятый часъ насъ ради плотію смерти вкусивый...'; Greek Ὁ ἐν τῇ ἐννάτῃ ὥρᾳ δι' ἡμᾶς σαρκὶ θανάτου γευσάμενος...), interspersed with verses from Psalm 118 (LXX Ps. 118:169, 170).

[^124]: Folio 37v provides the Christological Theotokion of the Ninth Hour ('Иже насъ ради рождейся отъ Дѣвы, и распятіе претерпѣвъ, Благій...'; Greek Ὁ δι' ἡμᾶς γεννηθεὶς ἐκ Παρθένου, καὶ σταύρωσιν ὑπομείνας, Ἀγαθέ...), the prayer of Azariah from the furnace of Babylon (Dan. 3:34–35 / LXX Pr. Azar. 11–12), forty repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy', and the Lenten Troparion of the Good Thief in Tone 8 ('Видя разбойникъ Начальника жизни на крестѣ висяща...').

[^125]: Folio 38r completes the Stavrotheotokion of the Ninth Hour ('Ягньца и Пастыря и Спаса міру на крестѣ зрящи...'), followed by forty repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy', the Prayer of the Hours ('Иже на всякое время...'), the Prayer of Saint Ephrem the Syrian with three great prostrations and twelve metanias, and introduces the ancient Mid-Hour of the Ninth Hour (Междочасіе 9-го часа / Interhorium Nonae) with three prostrations and Psalm 112 (LXX Ps. 112:1–4; 'Хвалите, отроцы, Господа...').

[^126]: Folio 38v completes Psalm 112 (LXX Ps. 112:4–9), and introduces the second psalm of the Mid-Hour of the Ninth Hour, Psalm 137 (LXX Ps. 137:1–4; 'Исповѣдаюся Тебѣ, Господи, всѣмъ сердцемъ моимъ...').

[^127]: Folio 39r reveals an epigraphic textual lacuna between fol. 38v and fol. 39r in this surviving exemplar: following the opening four verses of Psalm 137 on fol. 38v, fol. 39r opens directly with the concluding lines of the Mid-Hour supplication to Christ the Good Shepherd ('...грѣшныя, да не отлучиши мене стада Твоего, Пастырю добрый...'), followed by the Mid-Hour troparia ('Яко разбойникъ исповѣдаяся...' and 'Насъ ради распеншагося...'), thirty repetitions of 'Lord, have mercy', the Prayer of St. Ephrem, and the opening lines of the canonical Prayer of St. Basil the Great ('Владыко Господи Іисусе Христе Боже нашъ, долготерпѣливый о нашихъ согрѣшеніихъ...'; Greek Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ὁ μακροθυμήσας ἐπὶ τοῖς ἡμῶν πλημμελήмаσι...).

[^128]: Folio 39v continues the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great at the Mid-Hour of the Ninth Hour, preserving its profound penitential theology of the Crucifixion, the admission of human fragility and straying from the divine path, and the supplication for the mortification of carnal mind and the putting on of the new man created in righteousness.

[^129]: Folio 40r completes the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great with its Trinitarian doxology ('...и Тебѣ славу возсылаемъ, со Безначальнымъ Ти Отцемъ, и съ Пресвятымъ и Благимъ и Животворящимъ Ти Духомъ, нынѣ и присно и во вѣки вѣкомъ. Аминь'). It introduces the monumental office of Vespers with an ornate cinnabar title ('ЧИНЪ ВЕЧЕРНИ ПОЕМЫЯ') and detailed 15th-century monastic Typikon rubrics governing the sounding of the great semantron or bell by the lamp-lighter (кандилаптъ / candelaptes) following the hegumen's blessing.

[^130]: Folio 40v witnesses the transitional rubrics from the Ninth Hour to Vespers (Вечерня / Hesperinos), specifying the concluding prayers in the narthex (притворъ / pronaos), the ascent of the brethren into the temple after the priest's blessing, and introduces the Prooemiac or Introductory Psalm of Vespers, Psalm 103 (LXX Ps. 103:1–6; 'Благослови, душе моя, Господа...'). In this 15th-century Ruthenian monastic witness, the psalm is interspersed with ancient Studite refrains (припѣвы): 'Благословенъ еси, Господи' ('Blessed art Thou, O Lord') after the opening verse, and 'Дивна дѣла Твоя, Господи' ('Marvelous are Thy works, O Lord') following verse 4.

[^131]: Folio 41r continues Psalm 103 (LXX Ps. 103:7–17), celebrating God's providential ordering of the waters, the sustenance of the beasts of the field and the birds of heaven, and the gifts of wine, oil, and bread that gladden and strengthen the heart of man. It preserves the ancient choral refrain following verse 12: 'Слава Ти, Господи, сотворившему вся' ('Glory to Thee, O Lord, Who hast made all things!').

[^132]: Folio 41v continues Psalm 103 (LXX Ps. 103:18–28), praising the nocturnal cycle, the young lions seeking prey from God, the daytime labor of mankind, and the leviathan sporting in the vast sea. At the bottom of the leaf (line 19), Schweipolt Fiol's typesetters produced an anomalous corrupted line in cinnabar ('слава ти г҃и , анепепааипаньѣамене...'), caused by repetitive typesetting sorts and scrambled syllables anticipatory of the refrain completed on fol. 42r ('Слава Ти, Господи, наипаче сотворившему вся').

[^133]: Folio 42r completes Psalm 103 (LXX Ps. 103:29–35), resolving the typesetting corruption of the preceding leaf ('нааипаньѣ сътворившомоу вса...'), followed by three Alleluias with metanias, the Great Litany, and 15th-century Typikon rubrics regulating whether the Psalter Stichologia (the appointed evening Kathisma) is chanted or omitted, before advancing to the Lucernarium ('Господи, воззвахъ'). The signature at the bottom right marks the opening of quire 22 (к҃в).

[^134]: Folio 42v contains Psalm 140 (LXX Ps. 140:1–8), the foundational psalm of the Lucernarium (LXX Ps. 140; 'Господи, воззвахъ къ Тебѣ, услыши мя...'; Greek Κύριε, ἐκέκραξα πρὸς σέ, εἰσάκουσόν μου), designated in the left margin by the red numeral 'р҃м'. It preserves the ancient vocal refrain 'Услыши мя, Господи' ('Hear me, O Lord') following verse 1, and the solemn evening prayer of incense ('Да исправится молитва моя, яко кадило предъ Тобою...').

[^135]: Folio 43r concludes Psalm 140 (LXX Ps. 140:8–10) and introduces Psalm 141 (LXX Ps. 141:1–6; 'Гласомъ моимъ къ Господу воззвахъ...'; Greek Φωνῇ μου πρὸς Κύριον ἐκέκραξα), rubricated as the 'Разумъ Давыдовъ, внегда бы въ пещерѣ моляшеся' (Maskil of David, when he was in the cave praying; LXX Ps. 141), accompanied by the penitential penitential refrain 'Воззвахъ к Тебѣ, спаси мя' ('I cried unto Thee, save me!').

[^136]: Folio 43v concludes Psalm 141 (LXX Ps. 141:7; 'Изведи изъ темницы душу мою...'), and introduces Psalm 129 (LXX Ps. 129:1–8; 'Изъ глубины воззвахъ к Тебѣ, Господи...'; Greek Ἐκ βαθέων ἐκέκραξά σοι, Κύριε), appointed for the insertion of the evening Stichera. It witnesses the Christological refrain 'Христе Спасе мой, спаси мя' ('O Christ my Savior, save me!'), followed by the opening of Psalm 116 (LXX Ps. 116:1–2; 'Хвалите Господа, вси языцы...').

[^137]: Folio 44r completes Psalm 116 (LXX Ps. 116:2) and outlines the rubrical distribution of the six Stichera between the Octoechos and Menaion. It witnesses the ancient evening hymn of thanksgiving, 'Phos Hilaron' (Свѣте тихій / Joyous Light), bearing an explicit authorial attribution to the Hieromartyr Athenogenes ('Твореніе святаго священномученика Анфиногена'), collating with the testimony of St. Basil the Great (De Spiritu Sancto 29:73), followed by the Sunday evening Prokeimenon (LXX Ps. 133:1–2; 'Се нынѣ благословите Господа...').

[^138]: Folio 44v records the complete weekday cycle of evening Prokeimena (Monday through Saturday) with their appointed psalm verses (LXX Ps. 4:4, 22:6, 53:3, 120:2, 58:10, 92:1). It details the Typikon ceremonial for the appointed brother's reverences and the recitation of 'Сподоби, Господи' (Vouchsafe, O Lord), as well as the ancient monastic Lenten order of chanting 'Alleluia' in place of the prokeimenon when no festal troparion is appointed.

[^139]: Folio 45r details the antiphonal performance of the Lenten Alleluia at Vespers, prescribing the specific daily psalm verses chanted by alternating choirs (Monday: LXX Ps. 6:2; Tuesday: LXX Ps. 98:5; Wednesday: LXX Ps. 18:5; Thursday: LXX Ps. 98:5), concluding with the Doxology and three metanias before the holy doors. It preserves the opening petitions of the ancient evening hymn of supplication, 'Сподоби, Господи' (Vouchsafe, O Lord; Greek Καταξίωσον, Κύριε), based on Daniel 3:26 and Psalm 118:12.

[^140]: Folio 45v witnesses the conclusion of the evening hymn of supplication, 'Сподоби, Господи' (Vouchsafe, O Lord; Greek Καταξίωσον, Κύριε), with the Father Paul Doxology Standard ('unto ages of ages'), followed by the Litany of Supplication ('Исполнимъ вечернія молитвы наша', Greek Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσпеρινὴν δέησιν ἡμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ) and the Prayer at the Bowing of Heads with its priestly exclamation ('Буди держава царствія Твоего...'). It then introduces the Aposticha (стихиры на стиховнѣ / aposticha) with the weekday psalm verses from Psalm 122 (LXX Ps. 122:1–4; 'Къ Тебѣ возведохъ очи мои, живущему на небеси...').

[^141]: Folio 46r witnesses the conclusion of the evening Stichera and the Typikon ceremonial of the canonarch (канонархъ / кононархъ), who performs reverences in the center towards the holy icons and to both monastic choirs before returning to his stall. It contains the Canticle of Simeon the God-Receiver ('Нынѣ отпущаеши', Nunc Dimittis; Luke 2:29–32), the Trisagion prayers, the dismissal litany, and the ancient Lenten evening troparia opening with the Angelic Salutation, 'Богородице Дѣво, радуйся' (Ave Maria; Luke 1:28, 42), accompanied by solemn metanias (дл҃е а҃ = 1 prostration).

[^142]: Folio 46v continues the penitential evening troparia for fasting seasons: the Troparion to the Forerunner ('Крестителю Христовъ, тебѣ ся молимъ...') with a prostration, the Troparion to the Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs ('Молите за ны, святіи апостоли...') with a prostration, and the Sub Tuum Praesidium ('Подъ твое благоутробіе прибѣгаемъ, Богородице Дѣво...'), rubricated to be recited standing without prostration ('без мѣнія'). It records forty Kyrie eleisons, the blessing of the priest, and the ancient monastic intercessory prayer 'Небесный Царю' (O Heavenly King, strengthen our faithful sovereigns...).

[^143]: Folio 47r concludes the prayer 'Небесный Царю' and details the monastic execution of the Prayer of St. Ephrem the Syrian ('Господи и Владыко живота моего...'), prescribing 3 great prostrations, 12 intermediate metanias with the three-part silent prayer of repentance ('Боже, очисти мя грѣшнаго...'), and a final 16th great prostration with hands uplifted on high. The rubrics stipulate that this penitential order is observed during the Apostles' Fast, Dormition Fast, Nativity Fast, and throughout the year on Wednesdays, Fridays, and days with Alleluia, and regulates the transition of the brethren to the refectory for supper (трапеза).

[^144]: Folio 47v witnesses the ancient monastic Table Ritual (Чинъ трапезы), opening with the dining antiphon from Psalm 21 (LXX Ps. 21:27; 'Ядятъ нищіи и насытятся...'). Following the meal, it prescribes the ritual Elevation of the Panagia (Чинъ о возношеніи Панагіи / прѣтѧжа / прѣчиста), the bread dedicated to the Mother of God, accompanied by the Marian troparion 'Бысть чрево Твое святая трапеза...' (Thy womb became a holy table...), 'Честнѣйшую Херувимъ', and the thanksgiving verses from Psalm 91:5 and Psalm 4:7–8.

[^145]: Folio 48r concludes the post-prandial thanksgiving from Psalm 4:8–9, the superior's blessing ('Съ нами Богъ...'), and opens the Order of Small Compline (Чинъ о малой павечерници / Apodeipnon / Compline) with a prominent display title in red cinnabar ligatured script (вязь). The rubric defines the liturgical seasons and feasts when Small Compline is chanted: during All-Night Vigils, feasts of ranked Saints, post-feasts of the Mother of God, the Winter Paschaltide span from December 24 to January 14, and throughout Meatfare and Cheesefare weeks. The signature at the bottom right marks the opening of quire 23 (к҃г).

[^146]: Folio 48v continues Small Compline, prescribing Psalm 50, Psalm 69, and Psalm 142, the Lesser Doxology ('Слава въ вышнихъ Богу'), the Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos (Канонъ молебный Пресвятѣй Богородицѣ), and the appointed troparia according to the day (the Sunday Hypakoe, Festal Troparion, or the daily cycle: 'Боже отецъ нашихъ', 'Иже во всемъ мирѣ мученикъ Твоихъ', 'Со святыми упокой, Христе', 'Молитвами, Господи, всѣхъ святыхъ'). It concludes with the foundational nocturnal prayers of Paul of the Monastery of the Benefactress ('Нескверная, неблазная...') and Antiochus the Monk ('И даждь намъ, Владыко, на сонъ грядущимъ...').

[^147]: Folio 49r introduces the Order of Ordinary Compline (Чинъ обычныя павечерница) with a red cinnabar ligatured display heading (вязь), chanted throughout the year outside of Great Lent. It details the opening Trisagion, Psalm 90 ('Живый въ помощи Вышняго'), the Messianic hymn of the Prophet Isaiah ('С нами Богъ, разумѣйте, языцы, и покаряйтеся, яко с нами Богъ!'; Isaiah 8:9–9:6), the Cherubic hymn ('Безплотное естество Херувимское...'), the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed ('Вѣрую во единаго Бога...'), and the daily troparia.

[^148]: Folio 49v continues Ordinary Compline, providing the ancient nocturnal prayer of St. Basil the Great ('Господи, Господи, избави насъ отъ всякія стрѣлы летящія во дни...'), the three evening Psalms (Ps. 50, Ps. 69, Ps. 142), the Supplicatory Canon to the Mother of God, and the weekly cycle of evening troparia: Monday for the Archangels, Tuesday for the Forerunner, Wednesday and Friday for the Holy Cross, Thursday for the Apostles and St. Nicholas, followed by the patronal saint of the temple, forty Kyrie eleisons, and the General Prayer of the Hours ('Иже на всякое время...').

[^149]: Folio 50r concludes Ordinary Compline with the 3 great prostrations and 12 metanias of the Prayer of St. Ephrem, the nocturnal prayers of Paul of the Evergetis and Antiochus, the priest's dismissal, and the mutual forgiveness ceremonial between the superior and the brethren ('Благословите, отцы святіи, и простите мя грѣшнаго...'), followed by the evening litany and retirement to cells. At the bottom of the leaf, a magnificent red cinnabar display heading in ligatured script (вязь) inaugurates Great Compline for Great Lent ('Начало павечерници великои въ святую великую четыредесятницю'). The signature at the bottom right marks the opening of quire 24 (к҃д).

[^150]: Folio 50v witnesses the conclusion of the introductory Trisagion prayers of Great Compline (Великое повечерие) and the recitation of Psalm 69 (LXX Ps. 69; 'Боже, въ помощь мою воньми...'), followed by the crucial rubric for the Great Penitential Canon of St. Andrew of Crete (Канонъ великій святаго Андрея Критскаго). In ancient Studite and early Jerusalem Horologia, such as Fiol's 1491 witness, the Great Canon is divided across the first four days of Clean Week (Monday through Thursday) and chanted at Great Compline. The text explicitly directs: 'аще есть недѣля первая святаго поста, поемъ великій канонъ святаго Андрея Критскаго, раздѣляющи на 4 части, куюждо пѣснь, яко съвръшити въ 4 дни куюждо часть'.

[^151]: Folio 51r concludes the Lenten rubric for the Great Canon with the standard post-ode Marian hymnody ('Достойно есть' and 'Честнѣйшую Херувимъ') and initiates the first station of Great Compline with Psalm 4 (LXX Ps. 4; 'Внегда воззвахъ, услыша мя, Боже правды моея...'). The leaf concludes with the inscription for Psalm 6, exhibiting the epigraphic witness 'въ конецъ пѣніи о семомь' (concerning the eighth / octave, an archaic East Slavic scribal rendering or phonetic confusion for 'о осмомъ', Greek ὑπὲρ τῆς ὀγδόης). The quire signature or leaf coordination marks this as the opening of folio 51.

[^152]: Folio 51v contains the complete text of Psalm 6 (LXX Ps. 6; 'Господи, да не яростію Твоею обличиши мене...'), the first of the seven classical Penitential Psalms, expressing the soul's groaning, nocturnal weeping, and bodily languor in the face of spiritual death and divine judgment. The leaf closes with the rubricated cinnabar heading for Psalm 12 (LXX Ps. 12; 'Псаломъ Давыдовъ, 12').

[^153]: Folio 52r witnesses the complete text of Psalm 12 (LXX Ps. 12; 'Доколѣ, Господи, забудеши мя до конца...'), followed by the liturgical closure of the first tri-psalm unit of Great Compline: the Lesser Doxology ('Слава... И нынѣ...'), the threefold Alleluia with three prostrations ('Аллилуіа трижды, и дѣле три'), and three Kyrie eleisons ('Господи, помилуй, трижды'). It then commences the second tri-psalm group of the first station with Psalm 24 (LXX Ps. 24:1–3; 'Къ Тебѣ, Господи, воздвигохъ душу мою...'), preserving the opening acrostic petition of trust and redemption.

[^154]: Folio 52v continues Psalm 24 (LXX Ps. 24:4–14), setting forth David's supplicatory plea for divine guidance ('Пути Твоя, Господи, скажи ми...'), forgiveness of the sins of youth and ignorance ('Грѣхъ юности моея и невѣдѣнія моего не помяни...'), and the covenantal blessing upon the meek and God-fearing. The orthography consistently maintains archaic Ruthenian/Middle East Slavic features, including nasal reflexes and jers.

[^155]: Folio 53r witnesses the conclusion of Psalm 24 (LXX Ps. 24:15–22; 'Очи мои выну ко Господу...'), concluding with the national redemption of Israel ('Избави, Боже, Израиля отъ всѣхъ скорбей его'). It immediately introduces the third Psalm of this unit, Psalm 30 (LXX Ps. 30; 'Псаломъ Давыдовъ о исступленіи, тридесятый', Greek ψалмὸς τῷ Δαυΐδ, ἐκστάσεως, λ҃), beginning with David's cry of refuge: 'На Тя, Господи, уповахъ, да не постыжуся въ вѣкъ...' (LXX Ps. 30:1–3).

[^156]: Folio 53v continues Psalm 30 (LXX Ps. 30:3–11), featuring the celebrated Christological and Compline surrender verse: 'Въ руцѣ Твои предамъ душу мою; избавилъ мя еси, Господи, Боже истины' (Luke 23:46; Ps. 30:6). The text articulates the acute physical and psychological suffering of the psalmist ('изнеможе нищетою крѣпость моя, и кости моя смятошася'), underscoring the deep penitential ethos of Great Compline.

[^157]: Folio 54r continues Psalm 30 (LXX Ps. 30:12–20), chronicling the psalmist's alienation ('паче всѣхъ врагъ моихъ быхъ поношеніе... быхъ яко сосудъ погубленъ'), the conspiracy against his life, and his renewed confession of faith ('Азъ же на Тя, Господи, уповахъ: рѣхъ: Ты еси Богъ мой; въ руку Твоею жребіи мои'). It concludes with the encomium of God's abundant goodness reserved for those who fear Him.

[^158]: Folio 54v witnesses the conclusion of Psalm 30 (LXX Ps. 30:20–25; 'Благословенъ Господь, яко удиви милость Свою въ градѣ обьстоянія... Мужайтеся, и да крѣпится сердце ваше, вси уповающеи на Господа'). It then introduces Psalm 90, the climactic protective canticle of Compline, headed by the cinnabar title: 'Хвала пѣсни Давыдовы, 90' (Greek Αἶνος ᾠδῆς τῷ Δαυΐδ, ϟ҃), transcribing the opening declaration of divine defense under the wings of the Almighty (LXX Ps. 90:1–4).

[^159]: Folio 55r continues Psalm 90 (LXX Ps. 90:4–14), embodying the premier nocturnal apotropaic prayer of the Byzantine rite against the terror of night, the flying arrow, the pestilence, and the noonday demon ('отъ срѣща и бѣса полуденнаго'). It contains the angelic guardianship promise ('яко Ангеломъ Своимъ заповѣсть о тебѣ...') cited in the Temptation in the Wilderness (Matt. 4:6; Luke 4:10–11) and concludes with the opening phrase of the divine oracle: 'Яко на Мя упова, и избавлю и' (LXX Ps. 90:14).

[^160]: Folio 55v witnesses the conclusion of Psalm 90 (LXX Ps. 90:14–16; 'и покрыю и, яко позна имя Мое...'), completing the third Psalm of the first station of Great Compline (Великое повечерие). Following the Lesser Doxology, threefold Alleluia with three metanias, and three Kyrie eleisons, the rubric introduces the celebrated Old Testament Canticle of Isaiah (Isaiah 8:9–18, 9:2, 6–7): 'глаголи и ны: пѣснь пророчьства святаго пророка Исаіа'. The refrains 'яко с нами Богъ' (Greek ὅτι μεθ' ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός) are chanted antiphonally between the two choirs. The orthography exhibits typical early Cyrillic South Slavic/Middle East Slavic features with jers and nasal vowels.

[^161]: Folio 56r continues the Canticle of Isaiah ('Се азъ и дѣти, яже ми далъ Богъ... Отроча родися намъ, и Сынъ дасться намъ...'), preserving the Messianic titulature of Christ: 'Велика Свѣта Ангелъ, Чюденъ Совѣтникъ, Богъ крѣпокъ, Владыка, Князь миру, Отецъ будущаго вѣка'. After the Doxology and the final threefold refrain, the rubric directs: 'глаголи сіе 3, таже...' and introduces the first nocturnal troparion of Great Compline: 'День прешедъша благодаря Тя, Господи, вечеръ молюся, въ нощии безнаветіе подаждь ми, Спасе, и спаси мя'. The lower right margin displays the Cyrillic quire signature 'к҃е' (25).

[^162]: Folio 56v contains the two troparia of the first Compline triad ('День изъшедъ славословлю Тя, Владыко...' and 'День прешедъ пѣніемь славлю Тя, Святый...'), punctuated by 'Слава...' and 'И нынѣ...'. It then introduces the ancient hymn of the incorporeal orders ('Безплотное естество Херувимское, немолчными песньми славословитъ...'), invoking the Seraphim, angels, the Theotokos, the apostles, prophets, and martyrs to intercede for salvation before the indivisible Trinity.

[^163]: Folio 57r witnesses the conclusion of the hymn of the incorporeal powers with the Thrice-Holy invocation ('Святый, Святый, Святый, Трисвятый Господи, помилуй и спаси ны'). The rubric 'таже' immediately introduces the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Symbol of Faith ('Вѣрую въ единаго Бога, Отца Вседержителя...'), transcribing the Creed through the crucifixion and resurrection to Christ's second coming ('пакы грядоущаго съ славою судити живыимъ и мрътвыимъ'). Fiol's printed witness preserves ancient unrevised syntactic readings, such as 'при понтенстѣмь Пилатѣ'.

[^164]: Folio 57v concludes the Symbol of Faith ('Егоже царствію нѣсть конца... и жизни будущаго вѣка. Аминь') and proceeds to the supplicatory petitions of Great Compline, headed by the rubric: 'таже сіе: Пресвятая Владычице Богородице, всемилостивая, моли Бога о насъ (метаніе 1, и другый ликъ то же, метаніе 1; сице глаголетъ, и прочая святыхъ въздавая)'. Petitions follow to all heavenly powers, St. John the Forerunner, the apostles and martyrs, the venerable fathers and ecumenical doctors, and the invincible power of the Precious Cross ('Непобѣдимая божествьная сило честнаго и животворящаго Креста Господня, не остави насъ грѣшныхъ...').

[^165]: Folio 58r witnesses the concluding penitential cries ('Боже, милостивъ буди намъ грѣшныимъ... се же глаголи трищи, метанія 3'), the Trisagion prayers ('безъ дѣенія' / without prostrations), and following the Pater Noster, the Tone 2 troparia: 'Просвѣти очи мои, Христе Боже, да не когда усну въ смерть...' and 'Заступникъ души моей буди, Боже...'. The Theotokion 'Яко не имамы дерзновенія...' completes the triad. The rubric then provides: 'а се иныи тропари, гласъ 8, ихже поемъ предъ церквію на ючни презъ день' (which we chant before the church at Matins on ordinary days), displaying vernacular Middle Ukrainian/Ruthenian lexical influences ('ючня' for Matins, Polish jutrznia; 'презъ день' for during the daytime/weekdays). The quire signature 'к҃ѕ' (26) is marked at bottom right.

[^166]: Folio 58v continues the Tone 8 nocturnal troparia of Great Compline: 'Невидимыя врагы моя и неусыпаніе свѣси, Господи, и окаянныя плоти моея неможеніе вѣси, Создавый мя...'. Following the Psalm verse 'Призри и услыши мя, Господи Боже мой', it chants the terrifying meditation on the Last Judgment: 'Яко страшенъ судъ Твой, Господи, ангеломъ предстоящимъ, человѣкомъ вводимымъ, книгамъ разгибаемымъ, и дѣломъ испытаемымъ...'. Under 'Слава...', it begins the penitential hymn of the sinful woman: 'Сльзы ми дажь, Боже, якоже древле женѣ грѣшницѣ...'.

[^167]: Folio 59r concludes the hymn of the sinful woman ('да услышу и азъ благаго Твоего гласа: вѣра твоя спасе тя, иди въ миръ') and presents the Theotokion: 'Непостыдную, Богородице, надежду Твою имѣя, спасуся...'. After 40 Kyrie eleisons, the Lesser Doxology, and 'More honorable than the Cherubim', the priestly dismissal verse is invoked: 'За молитвы святыхъ...'. The rubric then introduces the classic nocturnal prayer of St. Basil the Great, here designated as 'Молитва сна' (Prayer of Sleep): 'Господи, избави ны отъ всякія стрѣлы летящая во дни...'.

[^168]: Folio 59v continues the Prayer of Sleep attributed to St. Basil the Great ('...поприще безъ порока преити, не искусомъ отъ злыхъ; избави ны отъ всякого смущенія и страха, иже отъ діавола напребывающаго...'). It implores divine custody over bodily passions and nocturnal fantasies ('остави же отъ насъ всяко мечтаніе неподобное и похоть врѣжуща'), closing with the Trinitarian doxology. The rubric then marks the transition to the Second Station of Great Compline: 'Пріидѣте, поклонимся, трижды, и метанія 3, псаломъ 50: Помилуй мя, Боже...'.

[^169]: Folio 60r concludes the incipit of Psalm 50 and introduces Psalm 101 (LXX Ps. 101:1–10) under the rubricated inscription: 'пѣснь въ умыслѣ: молитва нищаго, егда уныеть, предъ Господемь проліеть моленіе свое, 101' (Greek Προσευχὴ τῷ πτωχῷ, ὅταν ἀκηδιάσῃ...). David's lamentation over physical wasting, desert solitude, and mortal enemies is rendered with high fidelity. Notably, at verse 8 ('бдѣхъ и быхъ яко птица особящаяся на здѣ'), Fiol's 1491 witness exhibits the remarkable scribal variant 'забыи быхъ' ('I forgot [myself] / I was forgotten') rather than the canonical Byzantine/Slavonic 'бдѣхъ' (Greek ἠγρύπνησα, 'I watched / was sleepless').

[^170]: Folio 60v witnesses the central section of Psalm 101 (LXX Ps. 101:11–19; 'гнѣва Твоегѡ и ярости Твоея...'), continuing the lamentation of the afflicted penitent in the Second Station of Great Compline (Великое повечерие). The Psalmist's meditation contrasts mortal transience ('денне мои якѡ сѣнь оуклонишася, и язъ яко сѣно исхо́хъ') with divine eternity ('Ты же, Господи, въ вѣкы пребываеши...'). Fiol's 1491 Krakow print exhibits distinctive Early Cyrillic / Middle Ukrainian linguistic and orthographic traits, including the vernacular collective form 'каменне его̀' (Ukrainian каміння) and 'денне мои' alongside the archaic aorist 'исхо́хъ' (иссохохъ).

[^171]: Folio 61r continues Psalm 101 (LXX Ps. 101:19–27; '...лятъ Господа. Якѡ приниче съ высоты святыя своея...'). David proclaims the deliverance of the captives and the building of Zion ('раздрѣшити сыны оумръщвленыхъ, возвѣстити въ Сіонѣ имя Господне'). The folio witnesses the Messianic dialogue on the shortening of days ('оумаленіе денни моихъ возвѣсти мнѣ') and concludes with the cosmic contemplation of God's immutability over the transient heavens and earth ('въ начатъцѣхъ Ты, Господи, землю основа... та погыбнутъ, Ты же пребываеши').

[^172]: Folio 61v completes Psalm 101 (LXX Ps. 101:27–29; 'и вся яко риза обетьшають... Ты же тъжьдь еси, и лѣта Твоя не оскудѣютъ') and introduces the celebrated Apocryphal Canticle, the Prayer of Manasseh King of Judah, with the rubric in red ink: 'и посемь молитва Манасіа царя іоудейска'. The initial petition invokes the God of the Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob ('Господи Вседръжителю, Боже отѣцъ нашихъ...'). At line 18, Fiol's text preserves the variant 'ѡ лица славы Твоея' where Byzantine Greek witnesses read ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς δυνάμεώς σου ('before the face of Thy power'), preceding the identical formula 'вельлѣпота славы Твоея'.

[^173]: Folio 62r contains the heart of the Prayer of Manasseh, magnifying the unsearchable mercy of God ('безчисльная же и неизслѣдованная милость обѣщанія Твоего') and His appointment of repentance unto sinners rather than the righteous ('Ты убо, Господи Боже праведныхъ, нѣси положилъ покааніа праведнымъ Твоимъ, Аврааму и Исааку [и] Іакову... но положилъ еси покааніе мнѣ грѣшному'). The king confesses his innumerable transgressions exceeding the sands of the sea ('зане согрѣшихъ Ти паче числа пѣска морскаго') and his spiritual imprisonment under the heavy bonds of sin ('связанъ есмь многими узами').

[^174]: Folio 62v concludes the Prayer of Manasseh ('желѣзными, яко не возвести главы моея...'). The supplicant bows the knees of his heart ('приклоняю колѣнѣ сердца моего') and cries for pardon using the distinct archaic Ruthenian formula 'оради ми, Господи, оради ми' (Greek ἄνες μοι, remitte mihi / pardon me). At lines 16–17, Fiol's edition exhibits a notable scribal variant/misprint: 'въ вся дни живота Твое́го' ('all the days of Thy life') instead of the canonical 'живота моего' ('all the days of my life'). The prayer concludes with a full Trinitarian doxology.

[^175]: Folio 63r witnesses the rubrical transition from the Second to the Third Station of Great Compline. Following the Trisagion prayers and 'Our Father', the choir chants the Tone 6 penitential troparia: 'Помилуй насъ, Господи, помилуй насъ', 'Слава: Господи, помилуй насъ', and 'И нынѣ: Милосердія двери отверзи намъ'. Fiol's rubrics abbreviate the subsequent offices, cross-referencing prayers to other sections of the Horologion: 'пиши въ троичнѣ канонѣ' (read in the Triadic Canon), forty Kyrie eleisons, the Prayer at Every Time ('Молитва еже на всяко время'), the Prayer of St. Mardarios ('Владыко Боже, Отче Вседержителю...'), Psalms 69 and 142 ('пиши въ утренни' / written in Matins), the Lesser Doxology ('Слава въ вышнихъ Богу... писанъ по из-за псалмѣхъ'), and the Supplicatory Canon.

[^176]: Folio 63v presents the climactic choral dialogue of Great Compline: the hymn 'Господи силъ, с нами буди, иного бо развѣ Тебе помощника въ скорбехъ не имамы, Господи силъ, помилуй насъ' (Lord of hosts, be with us; for other helper in tribulations beside Thee we have not: Lord of hosts, have mercy on us), chanted antiphonally between the two choirs. The verses are taken from Psalm 150 (the Praise Psalms / Хвалитные псалмы), numbered explicitly in the rubric: 'хвалите Бога во святыхъ Его' (v. 1), 'хвалите Его на силахъ Его' (v. 2), 'хвалите Его во гласѣ трубнѣмъ' (v. 3), 'хвалите Его в тимпанѣ и лицѣ' (v. 4), and 'хвалите Его в кимвалѣхъ доброгласныхъ... всяко дыханіе да хвалитъ Господа' (v. 5), concluding with the full refrain.

[^177]: Folio 64r opens with the rubric for the joint choral chanting: 'съкупившеся оба лика вкупѣ, и глаголютъ со стихи высочайшимъ гласомъ' (Both choirs having gathered together, they say with verses in the highest voice), repeating the first verse and refrain of 'Lord of hosts, be with us'. Under 'Слава, гласъ 6', it gives the troparion of the saints' intercession: 'Господи, аще не быхомъ имѣли святыя Твоя молитвеники...'. Under 'И нынѣ', it provides the penitential Theotokion: 'Многая премножества моихъ, Богородице, прегрѣшеній...'. It also gives the short prayers: 'Всесвятая Богородице, во время живота моего не остави мене...' and 'Все упованіе мое к тебѣ возлагаю, Мати...'. At the bottom right margin, the printed quire signature 'к҃з' (27) is preserved.

[^178]: Folio 64v concludes the prayer to the Theotokos ('...Божія, сохрани мя въ своемъ крови') and, following forty Kyrie eleisons, introduces the classic evening prayer to the Mother of God with the rubric: 'таже молитва Марка священномоника' (Then, the prayer of Mark the Hieromonk; elsewhere attributed to Paul of Evergetis): 'Нескверная, неблазная, нетлѣнная, пречистая, Богоневѣсто Владычице...'. The prayer magnifies the Incarnation of the Word and petitions for the unmerited purification and defense of the soul amidst spiritual despondency.

[^179]: Folio 65r witnesses the second half of the Prayer of Mark the Hieromonk (Paul of Evergetis) to the Most Holy Theotokos ('Владыку и Господа матернимъ си дерзновеніемъ объемши умоли...'). It entreats the Virgin's maternal intercession to grant true repentance, to stand as a fervent protector throughout earthly life, to repel demonic assaults at the hour of death ('въ время исхода моего, окаянную ми душу соблюдающи, и темныя образы лукавыхъ бѣсовъ далече от нея отрѣвающи'), and to deliver the soul from eternal torment at the Last Judgment.

[^180]: Folio 65v completes the Prayer of Mark the Hieromonk (Paul of Evergetis) with the final Trinitarian doxology ('бл҃готію и чл҃колюбі́емь є́диноро́днаго сн҃а тво́его...'). Following the dismissal versicles, Fiol's rubric specifies the Lenten prostrations: three great metanias accompanied by the penitential Prayer of St. Ephrem the Syrian ('гн҃ и вл҃ко животоу мое́моу') and twelve minor bows ('ві, длєніи'), followed by the Trisagion prayers and twelve Kyrie eleisons. The leaf then introduces the beloved bedtime prayer of Great Compline under the rubric 'тажде · молитва · анти́ѡха мниха: ~' (Then, the prayer of Antiochus the Monk [of Mar Sabbas]): 'Да́жь намь вл҃ко на сонь гра́доущим покои дш҃и и тѣлоу...'.

[^181]: Folio 66r completes the Evening Prayer of Antiochus the Monk ('...кавно подвижимыꙗ и тѣла нашего въстаніа оу́стави...'). The rubric then directs the final litany-prayer of Great Compline: the brethren lie prostrate on their knees while the priest recites aloud the intercessory prayer: 'Вл҃ко многомл҃тиве, гн҃ іѵ҃ х҃е б҃е нашь, мл҃твами прчт҃ыꙗ вл҃дчца нашеа бц҃а...'. The bottom right margin bears the printed quire signature 'к҃и' (quire 28).

[^182]: Folio 66v concludes the Priest's Prayer of Absolution at Great Compline ('...нб҃ныі силы бесплътиы · чт҃наго и славнаго пр҃рока прч҃тчя...'). At line 5, the print witnesses a typographical repetition/slip ('оу́сътѧори мл҃твоу нашѫ' for 'оу́сътвори'). The folio records the mutual rite of forgiveness (чин прощения) between the celebrant ('Бл҃вите ѡ́ц҃и ст҃іи · и прости́те мѧ грѣшнаго...') and the brotherhood ('Б҃ъ да прости́ть тѧ и помилоу́еть'). At line 13, the Ruthenian form 'дн҃и́цю' (dialectal / archaic day/daytime, from день) is witnessed. The concluding rubrics direct the closing petitions of Great Compline for civil and ecclesiastical rulers and the brethren's pairwise reverence to the hegumen.

[^183]: Folio 67r concludes Great Compline with the rubric for monastic retirement to the cells in silence ('и ѡ́ходѧ въ своа кѣлеа со всѣцѣ мл҃чанніемь'). The folio marks a major structural division of the Horologion, introduced by a monumental cinnabar title in South Slavic / Early Cyrillic vyaz calligraphy: 'ТРОПАРИ И КОНДАЦИ ПРѢЗЪ ЛѢТО' (Troparia and Kontakia throughout the Year), using the distinctive Middle Ukrainian preposition 'презъ' (Ukrainian през, through/throughout). It inaugurates the weekly liturgical cycle (седмичный круг): Monday dedicated to the Bodiless Powers ('Нб҃ныі воинствъ а́рхістратиѕи...', with Theotokion and Kontakion) and Tuesday to the Holy Forerunner ('Па́мѧ праведнаго с похвалами...').

[^184]: Folio 67v completes the Tuesday Troparion of St. John the Forerunner ('...тѣмже поистиннѣ пострадавъ · радоуѧсѧ бл҃говѣстилъ є́си...'). It provides the Tuesday Theotokion ('Бж҃ію быхомъ є́стествоу причастници...') and the Tone 3 Kontakion to the Forerunner chanted to the famous podoben incipit of Romanos the Melodist ('д҃ва дн҃ь' / 'Дѣва днесь': 'Неплоды дн҃ь хв҃а прч҃тю ража́еть...'). Lines 14–19 introduce Wednesday, dedicated to the Precious Cross, giving the incipit of the Troparion of the Cross ('сп҃си ги люди своа' / LXX Ps. 27:9), the full Stavrotheotokion ('И жетвое ꙁастоупленіе стяжавше прч҃таа...'), and the incipit of the Tone 4 Kontakion ('въꙁнесы на кр҃т' / 'Вознесыйся на Крест волею').

[^185]: Folio 68r directs the reader for the full text of Wednesday's Kontakion to Matins ('пише въ тро́ре · въ оу́трници'). It then details the services for Thursday, dedicated to the Holy Apostles and St. Nicholas of Myra: Troparion of the Apostles (Tone 3, 'Ап҃ли ст҃іи молите мл҃тиваго б҃а...'), Troparion of St. Nicholas (Tone 4, 'Правило вѣрѣ и ѡ́браꙁь крости...'), Theotokion ('Слово ѡч҃ее...'), and the Romanos Kontakion of the Apostles (Tone 2, 'Твръдыꙗ и бг҃овѣщанныꙗ проповѣдателя...'). Friday rubrics repeat Wednesday's hymns of the Cross ('Въ пѧ · и́ ꙗ́къ въ сре па пи...'). The folio concludes with the opening of Saturday's All Saints Troparion ('Ап҃ли мч҃нци · пророци...').

[^186]: Folio 68v completes the Saturday All Saints Troparion ('...и ст҃ліє · прѣподобніи и праведніи...') and provides the liturgical memorials for the departed: the Troparion 'Помяни гн҃ яко благъ рабы своя...', the Theotokion 'Мати ст҃аа прѣчистаго свѣта...', and the incipit of the Kontakion of the Departed 'Съ ст҃ыми покои х҃е'. Lines 9–10 introduce the next monumental subsection under the cinnabar title: 'ТРОПАРИ ВОСКРЕСНИ И ИПАКОИ' (Resurrectional Troparia and Hypakoai of the Eight Tones). For Tone 1, it provides the Sunday Resurrectional Troparion ('Камени ꙁнаменаноу ѡ́ іоудеи...') and begins the Resurrectional Theotokion ('Гавриилоу провѣщавшю тебѣ дв҃ко радо...').

[^187]: Folio 69r concludes the Tone 1 Resurrectional Theotokion ('...мь кивотѣ · іакоже рече праведныи дв҃дь...') and gives the Tone 1 Hypakoe ('Раꙁбоиниче покааніе раи прокраде...'). It then witnesses Tone 2: the Resurrectional Troparion ('Егда съниде къ съ́мрти животе бесъ́мрътныи...'), the Dogmatic Theotokion ('Въся паче оума въся прѣславна...'), and the opening incipit of the Tone 2 Hypakoe ('По страсти шедьше на гробъ, помаꙁати тѣло твое...').

[^188]: Folio 69v concludes the Tone 2 Hypakoe ('...прѣчистое жены х҃е б҃е · видѣша а́гг҃лы въ гробѣ и оужасошѧ...'). It then provides the complete Sunday resurrectional cycle for Tone 3: the Troparion ('Да веселятся нб҃наа и радоуются ꙁемнаа...'), the Theotokion ('Тебе ходатаицю сп҃нію роду нашему, пое́мь бц҃е дв҃о...'), and the vivid angelic Hypakoe ('Оудивляꙗ видѣніемь ѡрошаа гланіи блистаяся а́гг҃ль...').

[^189]: Folio 70r contains the resurrectional cycle for Tone 4: the Troparion ('Свѣтлѫꙗ въскрсеніа проповѣдь...'), the Dogmatic Theotokion ('Еже ѡ вѣка оу́таеное...'), and the Hypakoe ('Иже твое́го прѣславнаго въстаніа...'). Lines 15–19 begin Tone 5 with the Resurrectional Troparion ('Съ беꙁнача́лное слово ѡц҃у и дх҃ови...'), concluding with Christ's voluntary crucifixion and endurance of death.

[^190]: Folio 70v completes the Tone 5 Resurrectional Troparion ('и въскр҃снти оу́мръшаꙗ въ славно́е въскрсеніе свое́'). It provides the Tone 5 Resurrectional Theotokion ('Ра́доуисѧ двери гн҃ꙗ непроходимаꙗ...') and the Hypakoe ('А́гг҃льскыимь ꙁрако́мь оу́мь съмѫщающе...'). Lines 14–19 introduce Tone 6 with its Resurrectional Troparion ('А́гг҃льскыꙗ силы на гробѣ тво́емь...'), concluding with the catchword incipit in cinnabar for the Tone 6 Theotokion ('Иже бл҃ве'). Red marginal letterings identify the structural genres ('б҃' for Theotokion, 'ѵ' for Hypakoe).

[^191]: Folio 71r concludes the Tone 6 Resurrectional Theotokion ('...ннаꙗ нарекыисѧ себѣ мт҃рь · пріиде на съдѫрть вѡльндыь съвѣтѡмь...'). The text displays distinctive archaic Middle Ukrainian orthography ('съдѫрть' / 'сѫдръть' for 'страсть'; 'вѡльндыь' for 'вольнымь'). Lines 6–10 give the Tone 6 Hypakoe ('Вл҃ною животворною ти съ́мрътїю х҃е...'). Lines 10–15 witness Tone 7: the Resurrectional Troparion ('Раꙁдроуши кр҃стѡмь свои́мь съ́мрътъ...') and the Dogmatic Theotokion ('Ꙗко нашемоу въскр҃нію сокровище...').

[^192]: Folio 71v opens with the Tone 7 Hypakoe ('И́же нашь ꙁракъ въспріе́млыи...'). Lines 3–7 contain the Tone 8 Resurrectional Troparion ('Съ вышинѣ съниде мл҃рде...'), followed by the Dogmatic Theotokion ('И́же на́ ради роже́исѧ ѡ дв҃ы...') and the Hypakoe ('Мѵ́роносица живодавномоу прѣстоаще гро́боу...'). The leaf concludes with the cinnabar rubric directing the singing of the two Sunday dismissal troparia after the Great Doxology ('сіа, тро́рѣ · по славословіи велицѣ , въ нп҃елѧ · сеже гл҃и').

[^193]: Folio 72r contains the two solemn Sunday troparia chanted following the Great Doxology: the troparion for odd tones (1, 3, 5, 7), 'Днесь спасение миру бысть...' (the opening words of which are trimmed at the top margin), and the troparion for even tones (2, 4, 6, 8), 'Въскр҃сь ѡ́ гроба, и́ оу́ꙁы растрѫꙁа...'. The bottom half of the leaf inaugurates a rare medieval calendar table recording the so-called 'Egyptian' or non-working days for September through January ('мц҃ь септе · а҃ до · ѕ҃ до · и҃ ве...'), noting whether the prohibition applies until noon ('до' / 'до полоудна'), in the evening ('ве'), or for the entire day ('весь'). The leaf bears the printed quire signature 'к҃ꙁ' (quire 27).

[^194]: Folio 72v completes the calendar table of Egyptian and fasting days for February through August. In lines 2–4, an extraordinary cinnabar monastic statute is embedded: 'вı же ѡтъ лаꙁарѧ въ в҃ · въ вт҃рѫ · срѣдоу · четвертокъ · пѧтокъ · всю · по клѧтвою ст҃ыхъ ѡц҃ь · ктѡ не празнуе' (Likewise from Lazarus Saturday: on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, all week, under the curse of the holy fathers, whosoever does not keep it as a feast). The second half of the folio opens a new hymnographic division under the monumental vyaz headpiece: 'БГ҃ОРОДИЧНЫ ПРОТИВО ГЛ҃ОУ ТРОРЕН КР҃Тꙋ И БЦ҃И' (Theotokia according to the Eight Tones: Troparia to the Cross and Theotokos), providing Tone 1.

[^195]: Folio 73r continues the dismissal Theotokia and Stavrotheotokia of the Eight Tones: Tone 2 ('Мт҃и ст҃аа прч҃тго свѣта...' and 'Чт҃ныи кр҃тъ сн҃а твое́го...'), Tone 3 ('Кождо и́де же сп҃саетсѧ...' and 'Жезлъ силы стяжавше кр҃то...'), and Tone 4 ('Стѣна непобѣдимаꙗ хрстіано́мъ є́си...'). Lines 17–19 begin the Tone 4 Stavrotheotokion in cinnabar ink ('На древѣ висѧще воꙁвѣи на сн҃а твоего...').

[^196]: Folio 73v completes the Tone 4 Stavrotheotokion ('...двы въсіꙗвыи въсемоу мироу х҃е б҃е...'). It provides Tone 5 Stavrotheotokion ('Кр҃тѡмь сы́на твоего · бг҃обл҃годатнаа...'), Tone 6 Theotokion ('Прѣславноу́ю х҃воу мт҃рь...') and Stavrotheotokion ('Тебе рожьшіа х҃е пр҃но дв҃аа...'), and opens Tone 7 with the Theotokion ('Радоуисѧ тебе въмѣстилаго на нб҃сехь въ оу́тробѣ...').

[^197]: Folio 74r concludes the Tone 7 Theotokion and gives its Stavrotheotokion ('Ра́доуисѧ бц҃е чт҃аа пр҃но дв҃о · на кр҃тѣ ꙁрящи...'). It then gives Tone 8: the Theotokion ('Тѧ стѣноу и пристанище и́мамы...') and Stavrotheotokion ('А́гнца и пастыря и сп҃са мироу...'). Lines 14–18 mark a monumental transition in the Fiol Horologion: the opening of the Menologion (Part III) under the decorative cinnabar vyaz title: 'МЦ҃Ь СЕПТЕВРИИ ИМЯ дній · л҃', marking the New Year / Indiction and the memory of St. Symeon the Stylite (September 1). The folio bears quire signature 'к҃ѳ' (quire 29).

[^198]: Folio 74v records the complete calendar commemorations for September 1 (St. Aeithalas, the 40 Holy Women and Deacon Ammoun, St. Callistus, Evodius, and Hermogenes, Joshua son of Nun, and the Great Fire of Constantinople) and sets forth the complete rubrics for Great Vespers of the Indiction and St. Symeon: Stichera at 'Lord, I have cried' (to the Indiction 3, to St. Symeon 3 Prosomoion and 4 automela), Doxasticon, Old Testament Paremias from Isaiah (61:1–9), Leviticus (26:3–12), and Wisdom (4:7–15), litanies, and the Aposticha.

[^199]: Folio 75r completes the Aposticha stichera and Psalm versicles (LXX Ps. 64:2, 5, 12) for September 1. It provides the Dismissal Troparion of the Indiction, Tone 2 ('И́же въсеꙗ твари съдѣтелю...'), the Troparion of St. Symeon the Stylite, Tone 1 ('Тръпѣнію стлъпь бысть...'), and the Dismissal Theotokion ('Ра́доуисѧ бл҃гослове́наа бц҃е дв҃о...').

[^200]: Folio 75v concludes the Dismissal Theotokion of the Indiction ('...бе бо въплъти сѧ и́ꙁбавитель мироу · є́дина є́си м҃ти · и дв҃а прѣблг҃вннаа...'). Lines 4–14 set forth the complete Matins rubrics for September 1: 'The Lord is God' in Tone 2, troparia, kathisma readings from the Life of St. Symeon, the canon order (Indiction, St. Symeon, and the 40 Holy Women) with the Katavasia of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross ('Крестъ начертавъ'), and the Kontakion of St. Symeon, Tone 2, Podoben: 'Seeking the Highest' ('Вышнихъ ищя': 'Съ вышьниими съвъкоупльшася...'). Lines 18–19 open the Praises with the incipit of the Tone 3 automelon 'Превѣчное Слово'.

[^201]: Folio 76r concludes the Liturgy of the Indiction and St. Symeon (September 1), detailing the Praises stichera, Doxology, prokeimena (LXX Ps. 146:5; LXX Ps. 115:6), Epistles (1 Tim. 2:1–7; Col. 3:12–16), Alleluia verses (LXX Ps. 64:2, 12; LXX Ps. 111:1), and Gospels (Lk. 4:16–22; Mt. 11:27–30). Lines 13–19 open September 2: the Holy Martyr Mamas and St. John the Faster, Patriarch of Constantinople, providing the Vespers stichera distribution, doxastica, and the opening incipit of the common Troparion of a Martyr, Tone 4 ('М҃чнкъ твои гн҃'). The folio bears the pencil numeral '76'.

[^202]: Folio 76v completes the Tone 4 Troparion of the Holy Martyr Mamas ('...мамонтъ · въ страдніи своє́мь вѣнець приꙗть нетлѣнныи ѿ тебе б҃а нашего...'). Lines 6–12 provide the dismissal Troparion of St. John the Faster, Tone 4 ('Правило вѣрѣ и́ ѡ́браꙁь кротости...'). Lines 12–18 provide the Matins order with the Kontakion of St. Mamas, Tone 3, Podoben: 'Today the Virgin' ('Дѣва днесь': 'Жеꙁломь ст҃е ѡ́т б҃а даннымь ти...'). Line 19 introduces the commemoration of September 3: Hieromartyr Anthimus of Nicomedia. The leaf bears the quire signature 'л҃' (quire 30).

[^203]: Folio 77r sets forth the liturgical order for September 3: Hieromartyr Anthimus of Nicomedia and Venerable Theoctistus. It gives the Vespers rubrics, the Troparion of the Hieromartyr, Tone 4 ('И́ нравомь причастникь и́ прѣтлѡмь намѣстникь а́пл҃ѡмь бывь...'), and the Troparion of the Venerable Father, Tone 8 ('Слъꙁами твоими источникь поустыни беꙁъчастное въꙁдѣлалъ є́си...'). Line 19 gives the Matins canon rubric and the incipit of the Kontakion in Tone 4, Podoben: 'Thou Who Wast Raised Up' ('Вознесыйся'). The folio bears the pencil numeral '77'.

[^204]: Folio 77v completes the Kontakion of St. Anthimus, Tone 4 ('Въ ст҃ителехъ бл҃гочт҃ивно поживъ...'), followed by the Liturgy apparatus (prokeimenon LXX Ps. 115:6, 3; Epistle Heb. 13:17–21; Alleluia LXX Ps. 131:9, LXX Ps. 111:1; Gospel Jn. 10:9–16). Lines 11–17 record the comprehensive calendar commemorations for September 4: St. Babylas of Antioch and 3 children, St. Babylas of Nicomedia and 84 children, the holy prophetesses Hermione and Eutychia (daughters of Philip the Deacon), and the holy Prophet Moses, opening their Vespers order. The leaf bears quire mark 'л҃'.

[^205]: Folio 78r concludes the September 4 service with the Troparion of the Holy Prophet Moses, Tone 2 ('Прр҃ка твое́го гн҃ па́мѧ праꙁноующе...'). It provides the Matins kontakia: to St. Babylas, Tone 8, Podoben: 'As the First-fruits' ('Яко начатки': 'Ꙗ҆ко бл҃гочт҃іа проповѣдника...'), and Tone 4, Podoben: 'Thou Hast Appeared Today' ('Явился еси': 'Веліа вѣра въ ср҃ци тво́емь...'). Lines 14–19 detail the Liturgy readings (LXX Ps. 15:3, 8; LXX Ps. 33:18; Mt. 10:32; LXX Ps. 32:1). The folio is numbered '78' in pencil.

[^206]: Folio 78v contains the full service for September 5: the Holy Prophet Zachariah, father of the Forerunner. It gives the Vespers order, the Troparion, Tone 1 ('Сщ҃енныꙗ ѡ́дежею ѡ́блечень...'), the Matins Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: 'Today the Virgin' ('Дѣва днесь': 'Прр҃къ дньсь іє́реи гн҃ьсъ ꙁахаріа...'), and the Liturgy apparatus (prokeimenon LXX Ps. 63:11, 2; Epistle Heb. 6:13–20; Alleluia LXX Ps. 96:11; Gospel Mt. 23:29–39). Lines 18–19 introduce the Commemoration of the Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Chonae (September 6). The leaf bears quire mark 'л҃'.

[^207]: Folio 79r contains the opening rubrics for September 6: the Commemoration of the Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Chonae (Colossae) and the Holy Martyr Eudoxius. It records the Vespers stichera, doxastica, and the Tone 4 Troparion of the Bodiless Powers ('Нб҃ныи воинствы а́рхистратиже...'). The bottom half of the leaf suffers from a severe diagonal tear (folio dissectum), resulting in the physical loss of the conclusion of the troparion and the opening Matins rubrics. The folio is numbered '79' in pencil.

[^208]: Folio 79v concludes the Liturgy of September 6 (prokeimenon LXX Ps. 103:4, 1; Epistle Heb. 2:2–10; Alleluia LXX Ps. 148:2, 5; Gospel Lk. 10:16–21; communion verse LXX Ps. 103:4). Lines 9–13 open September 7: the Forefeast of the Nativity of the Theotokos and the Holy Martyr Sozon. Owing to the diagonal tear on leaf 79, the lower half of the page is missing, truncating the Vespers stichera and dismissal troparia of the Forefeast.

[^209]: Folio 80r concludes the Forefeast of the Nativity of the Theotokos and St. Sozon (September 7), providing the Dismissal Theotokion conclusion, Troparion of the Martyr, Matins canon distribution, and the Kontakion of St. Sozon, Tone 2, Podoben: 'Seeking the Highest' ('Вышнихъ ищя': 'Ликъ честно состави мученику...'), followed by the Liturgy apparatus (prokeimenon LXX Ps. 63:11; Alleluia LXX Ps. 91:13; communion verse LXX Ps. 111:6). Lines 14–19 inaugurate the Great Feast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos (September 8), opening Small Vespers with its Tone 6 stichera and Aposticha. The leaf bears the quire signature 'л҃а' (quire 31) and pencil numeral '80'.

[^210]: Folio 80v concludes Small Vespers of the Nativity of the Theotokos (September 8), providing the Aposticha verses (LXX Ps. 44:11, 13) and the complete Dismissal Troparion, Tone 4 ('Рожство твоє бц҃е дв҃о · радость въꙁвѣсти въсеи въселенѣи · и́с тебе бо въсиꙗ слн҃це праведно́е хс҃ б҃ъ нашъ · раꙁроуши клѧтвоу · и́ дасть бл҃веніе · и́ оупраꙁнивъ съмрьть · дарова намъ животь вѣчныи :~').
